subject: Launch quote attribution, logo consent & press-quote approval playbook
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightclient.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: BrightClient redlines: MSA + order form (publicity & confidentiality)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again — attached are our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. The two items we need to solve before legal signs are: 1) the publicity/reference language (we want a narrow opt-in for press mentions and a short embargo window) and 2) logo use and brand lockup rights (we can supply the logos but need guidance on usage and attribution).

Specific asks from BrightClient:
- Publicity: BrightClient must approve any public quote and we request a 7-day review window (no automatic approval).
- Embargo: we propose a 21-day embargo after the first public mention.
- Logo: limited use for sales collateral and case study; no external marketing without separate permission.

Sending BrightClient_MSA_redlines.docx. Can you confirm Redwood's standard approach and whether you can accept our limited reference language?

Tom
Legal — BrightClient

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: BrightClient redlines: MSA + order form (publicity & confidentiality)

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding BrightClient's redlines (see attached). Short summary: they want strict approval on quotes (7-day review), a 21-day embargo window, and tight logo use.

Can legal review and propose counter-language that preserves our ability to reference the customer in deal flows and sales materials but addresses their approval window? Key constraints: we generally require a 48-hour quote approval SLA for customer stories and (where applicable) a 30-day embargo is our preferred maximum. If we must compress, we can accept 21 days but need explicit carveouts for anonymized metrics.

Actions:
- Kimberly: propose redline to Section 7 (Publicity) with explicit quote approval flow and an escrow for quote text (so we can continue pre-release comms).
- Marissa: if we accept logo usage, what do we need from BrightClient for our asset library? (file formats, brand guardrails).
- Priyom: add a single-line fallback in the Order Form that allows us to list BrightClient as a customer in sales decks (no quote) unless they explicitly opt-out.

I can loop in their PR contact if you want to iron out the attribution snippet.

—Sean
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightClient redlines: MSA + order form (publicity & confidentiality)

On Mon, May 31, 2027 at 10:02 AM sean_gallagher@redwood.ai wrote:
> Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding BrightClient's redlines (see attached). Short summary: they want strict approval on quotes (7-day review), a 21-day embargo window, and tight logo use.

Thanks Sean — I reviewed BrightClient_MSA_redlines.docx and drafted proposed language. High level: we can accept a 7-day approval window for customer quotes, provided we include a two-step approval flow (initial quote approval + final copy sign-off) and a maximum 21-day embargo only for joint press; we should keep a carveout allowing us to note the customer in anonymized performance metrics and in sales decks unless they opt out in writing.

Proposed redlines (summary):
- Publicity: Replace "BrightClient must approve" with "BrightClient shall have 7 business days to review and provide edits to any proposed public quote; absent response, the quote will be deemed approved for the limited use set out in the Order Form."
- Embargo: Agree to 21-day embargo for co-announcements, but add explicit exceptions for technical blog posts that do not reference BrightClient by name and for anonymized telemetry.
- Logo: Accept limited logo use for persistence in sales decks and case studies with required brand guidelines and a single approved lockup (BrightClient_logo_guidelines.pdf required). No other marketing channels without express written consent.

I attached redwood_publicity_template_v3.docx with markups. Two clarifying questions for BrightClient:
1) Can they accept our 48-hour accelerated sign-off process for critical marketing deadlines (we'll mark these in the mutual action plan)?
2) Do they require a separate asset escrow for logo files or is permission to store the approved assets sufficient?

If they insist on a strict 7-day hard-stop (no deemed approval), we should escalate to VP of Legal for an exception; that will slow signature.

-Kim
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@publishco.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, tom.reynolds@brightclient.com
Cc: press@publishco.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BrightClient redlines: MSA + order form (publicity & confidentiality)

Hi Sean / Tom,

Quick note from the PR side at PublishCo — if the customer requires a 7-day review that is fine, but we operate on a T+48 hour approval cadence for quotes to meet newsroom timelines. Could we land on the following workable flow?

- Draft quote submitted to BrightClient and to Redwood legal at t=0.
- BrightClient has 48 hours to provide edits for press quotes; if they need the full 7 days, they must notify us within 48 hours and provide expected date for final approval.
- For embargoes: 21 days for simultaneous joint press releases; PublishCo would like the option to publish a partner-authored technical blog earlier if it does not mention BrightClient by name.

Proposed attribution snippet we usually use: "BrightClient (customer) partnered with Redwood Inference to reduce inference costs by 6x — ‘quote here’ — Tom Reynolds, Head of Infrastructure, BrightClient."

We also need an approved high-resolution logo and a one-color lockup for dark backgrounds. Can Redwood or BrightClient confirm who will deliver the logo pack and the format?

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Editor, PublishCo

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightclient.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, elena@publishco.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightClient redlines: MSA + order form (publicity & confidentiality)

Tom / Kim / Marissa — thanks everyone. Summary and next steps below (agreeing to the middle ground so we can keep the rollout timeline intact):

Agreed points:
- Quote approval: BrightClient will have 48 hours for initial quote edits; if they need the full 7-day review window they must notify Redwood within that 48-hour window and provide a final approval date. (Legal to confirm wording in Order Form.)
- Embargo: 21-day embargo for joint press is accepted; Redwood retains right to publish anonymized metrics and product-tech posts that do not reference BrightClient by name.
- Logo: BrightClient will provide a high-res logo pack and a one-color lockup; Redwood will store assets in the marketing asset library. We will follow BrightClient_logo_guidelines.pdf for lockups.

Action items:
- Tom: please send BrightClient logo pack and confirm whether asset escrow is required or if permission to store approved assets suffices. Attach: BrightClient_MSA_redlines.docx (received).
- Kim: please formalize the agreed language (48-hour initial window with 7-day escalation option + 21-day embargo + anonymized metrics carveout) and update the Order Form redline.
- Marissa: prepare an entry in our asset library and a sample attribution snippet for PublishCo.
- Priyom: add the fallback line to the Order Form for anonymous listing in sales decks.

If legal is comfortable with the wording, we will route for signatures this week. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/record/DC-2027-1194.

—Sean
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightClient_MSA_redlines.docx
